ledger:2922: ## IndexedCone (narrower result: abstract ground family; identification with the physical wave family not formalized)
ledger:2923: 
ledger:2924: Formalizes `L:raw-block-indexed-cone` (`notes/integrated_raw_block_lower.tex`
ledger:2925: at `a284420`, lines 232-335) with its display
ledger:2926: `E:raw-block-positive-product`: for `0 < rho < 1/2` there are an integer
ledger:2927: `B >= 1` and `omega, eps_op > 0`, and `c_* = a_* j_*/4 > 0`, such that the
ledger:2928: product lower bound holds for every `N >= 1`, every `omega`-adjacent chain in
ledger:2929: `I = [0,1]` and every operator family `eps_op`-close to the block flows. The
ledger:2930: whole conclusion is proved, including the exact constant
ledger:2931: `c_* = a_* j_*/4`. The lemma uses the ground family of
ledger:2932: `S:compact-mean-family` (`notes/integrated_compact_mean_family.tex`, the
ledger:2933: C16 results), which is not formalized; its outputs are supplied as ONE
ledger:2934: hypothesis structure `GroundFamily F` over an arbitrary real normed space
ledger:2935: `F`, with these fields (TeX lines at `a284420`):
ledger:2936: 
ledger:2937: - `P`, `e`, `ell`, `lam`: the flows `P_sigma(t)` (line 17,
ledger:2938:   `E:compact-F-block`), the growing vectors `e_sigma` and duals
ledger:2939:   `ell_sigma` (`E:compact-F-projection`, lines 270-272) and the rates
ledger:2940:   `lambda_sigma` (`P:compact-ground-family`, line 48); `e0` and `obs` are
ledger:2941:   the data `e_0` and the bounded observable `O_phi`
ledger:2942:   (`S:actual-raw-block-lower`, lines 16-17); `d0` is the gap `d_0` (`E:compact-rate-gap`).
ledger:2943: - `lam_pos`: `lambda_sigma > 0` on `I`, a weakening of
ledger:2944:   `sqrt(eps) <= lambda_sigma` in `E:compact-rate-gap` (line 51).
ledger:2945: - `ell_e`, `P_Pi`, `Pi_P`: `ell_sigma(e_sigma) = 1` and
ledger:2946:   `P_sigma(t) Pi_sigma = Pi_sigma P_sigma(t) = e^(lambda_sigma t) Pi_sigma`
ledger:2947:   for `t >= 0`, exactly `E:compact-F-eigen` (lines 277-281), with
ledger:2948:   `Pi_sigma = e_sigma ell_sigma`.
ledger:2949: - `d0_pos`, `normalized_complement`: `d_0 > 0` and, for every
ledger:2950:   `0 < eta < d_0`, a `C` with
ledger:2951:   `||e^(-lambda_sigma t) P_sigma(t) Q_sigma|| <= C e^(-eta t)` for all
ledger:2952:   `sigma` in `I` and `t >= 0`, exactly `E:compact-normalized-complement`
ledger:2953:   (`P:compact-F-complement`, lines 344-348). `d_0` is abstract: its
ledger:2954:   identification with `inf_I(lambda_sigma - mu_sigma)` is not needed.
ledger:2955: - `e_cont`, `ell_cont`: norm continuity of `sigma -> e_sigma` and
ledger:2956:   `sigma -> ell_sigma` on `I` (`P:compact-F-projection`, lines 275-276).
ledger:2957:   Continuity and uniform boundedness of `Pi_sigma`, and boundedness of
ledger:2958:   `e`, `ell`, are derived (`Pi_bounded_continuous`), not assumed.
ledger:2959: - `margin_ell`, `margin_obs`: `0 < inf_I ell_sigma(e_0)` and
ledger:2960:   `0 < inf_I O_phi(e_sigma)`, exactly `E:compact-positive-margins`
ledger:2961:   (lines 283-286).
ledger:2962: 
ledger:2963: Every field is a displayed conclusion of `P:compact-ground-family`,
ledger:2964: `P:compact-F-projection` or `P:compact-F-complement`, or a weakening of one,
ledger:2965: so the structure is no stronger than C16. `scalarFamily` shows it is
ledger:2966: satisfiable. The proof is the TeX cone induction (entrance, rebase, full
ledger:2967: block, terminal) with the TeX's order of constant choices.
ledger:2968: `ConeConstants` records constants satisfying relaxed, sufficient versions
ledger:2969: of the TeX's inequalities (lines 254-281): the margins `a`, `j` are any
ledger:2970: positive lower bounds of `ell_sigma(e_0)` and `O_phi(e_sigma)` on `I` (not
ledger:2971: necessarily the infima `a_*`, `j_*`), `C_gap`, `eta_gap`, `nu` need only be
ledger:2972: `>= 0` (the TeX takes `C_gap >= 1`, `eta_gap > 0`, `nu > 0`), and `M_e`,
ledger:2973: `M_ell`, `M_P`, `H` are any nonnegative bounds (the TeX takes
ledger:2974: `max(1, sup)`). `positive_product_of_constants` proves the product bound
ledger:2975: for any such constants, with `c_* = a j/4`, and `exists_coneConstants`
ledger:2976: constructs them with the TeX's choices where needed (`C_gap >= 1`,
ledger:2977: `eta_gap = d_0/2`, positive `nu`) and with `a = a_*` and `j = j_*`; the
ledger:2978: starred constants in the final result come from this specialization. Side conditions made explicit: the TeX fixes
ledger:2979: `E_0 = ||e_0|| = 1`, whereas Lean allows any `||e_0||` (a generalization);
ledger:2980: the families are `D : N -> R -> (F ->L F)` with closeness required only for
ledger:2981: `m <= N` and `u` in `[0, B]`, and nothing else is assumed, as TeX line 249
ledger:2982: says. The product `D_N(u) D_(N-1)(B)...D_0(B) e_0` is
ledger:2983: `D N u (chainState D B e0 N)`. The wrapper `indexed_cone_paper` carries
ledger:2984: the section's standing hypotheses (a nonzero `Gamma` satisfying `H:homog`,
ledger:2985: lines 4-9) unused: the lemma depends on `Gamma` only through the ground

ledger:2987: phase space and its projections) is not formalized, so the link of `G` to
ledger:2988: `Gamma` is by documentation only.

ledger:5008 Formalizes `P:masked-quotient-obstruction` (A physical mask need not preserve
ledger:5009 noise-null tests) of `S:masked-covariance`
ledger:5010 (`notes/integrated_covariance_foundation.tex` at `a284420`, statement lines

ledger:5017 that `Gamma0 != 0` (the section's standing assumption, lines 5-6, holds for
ledger:5018 this `Gamma`), and that some real `C^infinity` compactly supported mask
ledger:5019 `zeta` on `R^2` admits no real `C` with
ledger:5020 `covW a Gamma0 (zeta F) <= C covW a Gamma0 F` for every test `F` with
ledger:5021 `IsTest T F`. `masked_quotient_obstruction` states the proof's computation
ledger:5022 with the explicit witnesses `zeta = chi(x_1) chi(x_2)`,
ledger:5023 `g = chi(x_1) chi''(x_2)` (`gtest`) and a bump `tau` supported in `(0,T)`
ledger:5024 (the proof chooses `tau` nonnegative and nonzero; the exported existential
ledger:5025 records `IsTest (tau g)`, temporal integrability and positive `timeQ`, not

ledger:5027 integrand it evaluates, `V(g) = 0`, `V(zeta g) = J_chi I_chi^2`,
ledger:5028 `covW(F) = 0` and `covW(zeta F) = norm(tau)_a^2 J_chi I_chi^2 > 0`.

ledger:5030 Definitional boundary (D1). The noise `W` is not constructed. `E W(F)^2` is
ledger:5031 read as the covariance functional of `E:cov`
ledger:5032 (`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `a284420`, lines
ledger:5033 219-222): `covW a Gamma F = int_t int_s |t-s|^(-a) int Gamma(dz) int F(t,x)
ledger:5034 F(s,x-z) dx`, iterated Lean Bochner integrals with time over `R` (equal to
ledger:5035 `[0,T]^2` for the tests used). Because a Bochner integral of a
ledger:5036 non-integrable function is `0`, the values `0` and `> 0` of the witnesses
ledger:5037 come with integrability conclusions (time integrand on `R x R`, spatial
ledger:5038 integrands for every `z` and against `Gamma0`), so they are genuine.
ledger:5039 
ledger:5040 Abstractions. "Compact smooth test `F`" (line 262) is `IsTest T F`:
ledger:5041 `(t,x) -> F t x` is `C^infinity` with compact support and vanishes unless
ledger:5042 `t in (0,T)`. This restricts the tests, so the nonexistence of `C` is
ledger:5043 stronger than over all compact smooth tests. `C` ranges over all reals.
ledger:5044 `Gamma = delta_0(dx_1) dx_2` is `lineMeasure e2`, the pushforward of
ledger:5045 Lebesgue measure under `t -> t e_2`; the plane `R^2` is
ledger:5046 `EuclideanSpace R (Fin 2)` with coordinates through the volume-preserving
ledger:5047 `plane : R x R -> R^2`. `chi` is Mathlib's `ContDiffBump` with radii `1` and
ledger:5048 `2` (equal to `1` on `[-1,1]`, `0` outside `(-2,2)`); the TeX's explicit
ledger:5049 formula (lines 276-279) is introduced "for example", and evenness of `chi`
ledger:5050 and `J_chi >= 2` are not used.

ledger:5054 continuous compactly supported `g` through the substitution `x = y + t e_2`

ledger:5056 bound `PlaneDecay`). Positive definiteness of `Gamma` (line 268) is proved

ledger:5061 `Phi(u) = int phi(u,v) dv`, whose Fourier transform is the restriction of the
ledger:5062 two-dimensional Fourier transform of `phi` to the first axis; the Schwartz
ledger:5063 decay of that restriction gives the integrability inversion needs. The

ledger:5179 `N + 1 <= 2/(delta B)`, `R_delta <= 3/delta` and the radius substitution.
ledger:5180 `C^theta([0,B];E)` is represented explicitly, following the manuscript's
ledger:5181 definition (`notes/integrated_actual_operator_driver.tex`, "the supremum norm
ledger:5182 plus the theta-Holder seminorm"). `supNorm` is the real supremum of `||f t||`
ledger:5183 over `[0,B]`, `holderSemi` is the real supremum of
ledger:5184 `||f t - f s|| / |t - s|^theta` over `s != t` in `[0,B]`, `holderNorm` is
ledger:5185 their sum, and `IsCHolder` (membership in `C^theta`) says both sets are bounded
ledger:5186 above. Mathlib's `HolderWith` is a predicate about a constant on the whole
ledger:5187 domain, not a norm on `[0,B]`, so it was not used. A real `sSup` of an
ledger:5188 unbounded set is `0` in Lean, so `holderNorm` is meaningful only for paths with
ledger:5189 `IsCHolder`. The supplied input requires this almost surely for `M_m`, and
ledger:5190 `stopped_isCHolder` gives it for the stopped paths. Paths are functions
ledger:5191 `R -> E` into a real normed space; only their values on `[0,B]` enter. The
ledger:5192 stochastic objects `W`, `Y_m`, `M_R` and the deterministic projection are
ledger:5193 abstracted to an arbitrary family of random paths `M m : Omega -> R -> E`, so
ledger:5194 the bounds are uniform in the projection, as the proposition states. The only
ledger:5195 manuscript input is the moment bound of `C:radius-covariance-residuals` (with
ledger:5196 `C = 1`, `v = p`; it rests on `P:radius-actual-moments`). It is a hypothesis
ledger:5197 on the unstopped paths `M_m = M_R(Y_m)`: almost surely `IsCHolder`, the `p`th
ledger:5198 power of the `C^theta` norm is integrable, and
ledger:5199 `(E ||M_m||_{C^theta}^p)^(1/p) <= C sqrt(p) R^(d/Q)`. Taking the input on
ledger:5200 `M_m` rather than on `X_m` means the stopping and the factor `g_delta` are

ledger:5202 measure, and `hXmeas` says `omega -> ||X_m(omega)||_{C^theta}` is

ledger:6873 What is formalized. (1) The per-frequency free matrix `W_t(xi)` of lines
ledger:6874 70-78 (`freeMatrix`, `freeMatrixAt`), written with the continuous sine
ledger:6875 quotient `t sinc(tk)` so that its value at `xi = 0` is the TeX's matrix

ledger:6895 Abstractions and supplied inputs. `E` is an abstract nonzero real Hilbert

ledger:6897 group law), an isometry `R` with `S_E(-h) = R S_E(h) R`, and isometries

ledger:7420 **`L:positive-series-type`** (statement lines 7222-7234, proof lines

ledger:7423 
ledger:7424 - The hypotheses are `nu >= 1`, `c_k >= 0` and `c_0 = 1`. "`F(z) < inf` for
ledger:7425   every `z >= 0`" is stated as summability of `k -> c_k z^k`.

### UniformSeriesTail
ledger:7547 ## UniformSeriesTail (narrower result: `L:uniform-series-tail` for an abstract `L^2` family with the two facts of `L:terminal-wick` supplied; identification with the terminal-chain terms not formalized)
ledger:7548 
ledger:7549 Formalizes `L:uniform-series-tail` (`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex`
ledger:7550 at `a284420`; statement lines 3703-3727 with the display
ledger:7551 `E:uniform-series-tail`, lines 3718-3724; proof lines 3729-3748), with every
ledger:7552 conclusion proved and one supplied input from `L:terminal-wick` (lines
ledger:7553 3600-3645), the structure `TerminalWickInput`. The TeX proof cites exactly two
ledger:7554 facts from `L:terminal-wick` (lines 3730-3731): absolute `L^2` convergence of
ledger:7555 every regularized series and nonnegative mixed moments. `TerminalWickInput mu Y r`
ledger:7556 states these two facts for one family `Y : N -> L^2` and the given `r`:
ledger:7557 `sum_n ||r^n Y_n||_2 < infinity` (`L:terminal-wick` gives it for every real or
ledger:7558 complex `r`, lines 3643-3644) and `E[Y_m Y_n] >= 0` for all `m, n` (its Wick
ledger:7559 formula with nonnegative pairing integrals when the covariance is nonnegative,
ledger:7560 and zero when `m + n` is odd, lines 3638-3641). Nothing else about the Gaussian
ledger:7561 field, the chain measures `g_n^{T,x}` or the Wick formula is used, so the Lean
ledger:7562 statements hold for an arbitrary family of real `L^2(Omega)` elements with these
ledger:7563 two facts. For the chain integrals `Y_n` of a centered Gaussian field with
ledger:7564 nonnegative covariance, `TerminalWick.terminalWickInput_of_nonneg` (wave L8)
ledger:7565 proves `TerminalWickInput` from that lemma's own inputs, and
ledger:7566 `L8Completed.uniform_series_tail_terminal_wick_paper` composes the two; the
ledger:7567 identification of the regularized family `Y_n^{eps,delta}` with such terms is
ledger:7568 not formalized. The
ledger:7569 fixed point `(T,x)` is implicit in the family. `L^2(Omega)` is Mathlib's
ledger:7570 `Lp R 2 mu` (real-valued), `E|f|^2` is written as the Bochner integral of
ledger:7571 `f(omega)^2` (equal to `||f||^2` by `integral_sq_eq_norm_sq`, a genuine
ledger:7572 integral), `E[fg]` as the integral of `f(omega) g(omega)` (equal to the inner
ledger:7573 product by `integral_mul_eq_inner`), `B_r^{1/2}` as `Real.sqrt B`, `r^{-n}` as
ledger:7574 `(r^n)^(-1)` and the tail `sum_{n>N} Z_n` as `tsum_n Z (n + (N+1))`.
ledger:7575 `uniform_series_tail_paper` takes the regularized terms as `Y eps delta n` for
ledger:7576 real `eps, delta`, assumes `r > 1`, `TerminalWickInput` and
ledger:7577 `E|u^{eps,delta}(r)|^2 <= B` for every `eps, delta > 0` (the uniform bound
ledger:7578 `sup_{eps,delta>0} E|u^{eps,delta}(r)|^2 <= B_r`), and `Y^{eps,delta}_n -> X_n` in
ledger:7579 `L^2` for each `n`, where `eps, delta down to 0` is read as the joint limit along
ledger:7580 the product filter `nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0) x nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0)` (other readings,
ledger:7581 such as iterated limits, are not stated). It proves seven conjuncts: absolute
ledger:7582 convergence of `sum X_n`; `u^{eps,delta}(1) = tsum_n Y^{eps,delta}_n -> u = tsum_n X_n`
ledger:7583 in `L^2` along that filter; the two term bounds and the two tail bounds of
ledger:7584 `E:uniform-series-tail`, the bounds for `Y` for every `eps, delta > 0`; and
ledger:7585 absolute convergence of each `sum_n Y^{eps,delta}_n` ("including absolute
ledger:7586 convergence", lines 3735-3736). `uniform_series_tail_second_moment_paper` proves the
ledger:7587 last sentence (lines 3725-3726): if also `E|u^{eps,delta}(1)|^2 <= B_1` for all
ledger:7588 `eps, delta > 0`, then `E|u|^2 <= B_1`. The probability measure
ledger:7589 (`IsProbabilityMeasure mu`) is the manuscript's setting and is carried but not
ledger:7590 used by either wrapper. The general forms `uniform_series_tail` and
ledger:7591 `uniform_series_tail_second_moment` hold in any complete real inner product
ledger:7592 space, for any index type of regularizations and any nontrivial filter, with the
ledger:7593 hypotheses required only eventually along the filter. Proof route: the term
ledger:7594 bound is the TeX's (the double sum `E|u(r)|^2 = sum_{m,n} r^{m+n} E[Y_m Y_n]`
ledger:7595 dominates its diagonal term, `norm_sq_le_of_inner_nonneg`), and the tail bounds
ledger:7596 are the geometric series and the triangle inequality (`tail_bound`). The limit
ledger:7597 `u^{eps,delta}(1) -> u` is proved by Mathlib's dominated convergence for series
ledger:7598 (`tendsto_tsum_of_dominated_convergence`) with the summable majorant
ledger:7599 `B^{1/2} r^{-n}`, instead of the TeX's explicit head/tail split at level `N`
ledger:7600 (lines 3738-3745), which uses the same majorant. No conclusion is narrower than
ledger:7601 the TeX. Junk values are not reached: the scaled series is absolutely summable by
ledger:7602 hypothesis and the unscaled ones are proved absolutely summable, so every
ledger:7603 `tsum` is a genuine sum; `B >= 0` follows from the moment bound, so
ledger:7604 `Real.sqrt B` is the true square root; `r > 1` makes `(r^n)^(-1)` and
ledger:7605 `1 - r^(-1)` positive. Not formalized: the regularized family itself (the terms
ledger:7606 `Y_n^{eps,delta}` as terms of `L:terminal-wick`) and the application of the
ledger:7607 lemma to the regularized solution in later proofs; `L:terminal-wick` is in
ledger:7608 `TerminalWick`, with its own inputs.

### VariationalDilation
ledger:7626 ## VariationalDilation (narrower result: `L:variational-control-dilation`, rate and variance identification not formalized)
ledger:7627 
ledger:7628 Formalizes Lemma `L:variational-control-dilation` (Radon and Rayleigh
ledger:7629 dilation; `notes/integrated_unmasked_variational.tex` lines 225-268 at
ledger:7630 `a284420`) together with the definitions it uses, in two modules:
ledger:7631 `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/WeakSobolev.lean` (a hand-built real Sobolev
ledger:7632 space and the real Rayleigh value set) and
ledger:7633 `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/VariationalDilation.lean` (the control class,
ledger:7634 the dilation, the mean, variance, rate and integrated rate, and the lemma).
ledger:7635 The wrapper `variational_control_dilation_paper` states the lemma with the
ledger:7636 section's standing hypotheses (line 4: a nonzero covariance satisfying
ledger:7637 `H:homog`, modelled by `HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance`, with `a = alpha0`):
ledger:7638 for `r > 0`, `D_r` is a bijection of the class with inverse `D_(1/r)`, and the
ledger:7639 four identities of `E:variational-dilation-values` hold. Nothing is supplied as
ledger:7640 a hypothesis.
ledger:7641 
ledger:7642 Abstractions and why they are faithful.
ledger:7643 The class `E:variational-positive-class` (lines 5-10) consists of smooth
ledger:7644 functions on `R x R^d` with compact support inside `(0,1) x R^d`, i.e. elements
ledger:7645 of `C_c^infinity((0,1) x R^d)` extended by zero. `CPos_nonempty` proves that
ledger:7646 the class is nonempty (lines 13-17) using a different bump. The mean
ledger:7647 `h_{Psi,s}` and the variance `v_Psi` are the
ledger:7648 displays `E:compact-raw-mean` and `E:compact-raw-cost`
ledger:7649 (`notes/integrated_compact_mean_family.tex` lines 402-412), with
ledger:7650 `(Gamma * phi)(x) = int phi(x-y) Gamma(dy)` and `int_0^1` taken over
ledger:7651 `Ioo 0 1`. Mathlib has no Sobolev spaces, so `WeakSobolev` defines
ledger:7652 `H^1(R^d; R)` by weak gradients (`int f d_v phi = -int <g,v> phi` for every
ledger:7653 test function `phi` and direction `v`). It proves that an `L^2` weak gradient
ledger:7654 is unique a.e. (`weakGradient_ae_unique`), so a Rayleigh set built from pairs
ledger:7655 `(f, g)` is the manuscript's set of `f`.
ledger:7656 
ledger:7657 The rate `lambda_{Psi,s}` is defined in Lean by the real Rayleigh form
ledger:7658 `E:variational-real-rayleigh`: `rate = sqrt(sSup R_s)`, where `R_s` is the set
ledger:7659 of values `int h_s f^2 - ||grad f||_2^2` over unit `f in H^1(R^d; R)`. The
ledger:7660 manuscript's primary definition is `lambda = sqrt(-E_s)`, with `E_s` the
ledger:7661 spectral bottom of the self-adjoint `-Delta - h_s` on `H^2`. The manuscript
ledger:7662 proves that the two agree (`P:variational-unmasked-rate`), but that equality is
